page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.vgn6i-m4-vws.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server configuration featuring a fractional NVIDIA T4 graphics processor (0.25 slice with 4 GB of VRAM). It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz across 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores with hyperthreading) and 23.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.75 GB per vCPU. Network throughput is provisioned with a 2 Gbps baseline, and the instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate entry-tier computational throughput. The instance recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 904.0 and a multi-core score of 2011.0, with a PassMark CPU score of 3597.24, ranking in the lower 10% to 25% of evaluated systems. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 19.82 GB/sec and write bandwidth peaked at 18.77 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning workloads, inference testing using a small 135M parameter language model achieved 233.71 tokens/sec for prompt ingestion and 64.28 tokens/sec during token generation.

Cost efficiency is centered on the fractional GPU allocation. By partitioning an enterprise-grade NVIDIA T4 into a quarter slice, the instance reduces the resource footprint compared to provisioning a full discrete GPU. The architectural trade-off is limited CPU compute and unexceptional uncached memory bandwidth, which restricts overall data throughput. Furthermore, the absence of local NVMe storage places I/O dependencies on network-attached storage performance.

The ecs.vgn6i-m4-vws.xlarge instance fits low-to-medium intensity graphical applications, virtual workstation sessions, remote 3D visualization, GPU software development, and lightweight machine learning inference pipelines that require minimal VRAM.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.vgn6i-m4-vws.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for light graphical and acceleration tasks. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores), 23.0 GB of RAM, and a fractional 0.25 NVIDIA T4 GPU with 4 GB of dedicated VRAM. The platform includes a 2 Gbps baseline network interface and relies on remote storage, offering no local disks. In synthetic testing, the instance exhibits modest CPU output, scoring 904.0 in single-core Geekbench and 3597.24 in PassMark CPU evaluations, paired with an uncached memory read speed of 19.82 GB/sec. With its fractional GPU profile, it delivers economical entry into hardware acceleration without requiring a dedicated discrete accelerator. The instance suits virtual workstation environments, entry-level 3D visualization, lightweight machine learning inference, and graphics-enabled development.
